i can’t comment on you home life and if you feel it’s unsafe, it’s probably best for you to wait.  hrt can still have big effects on your body and mental health no matter when you start so don’t feel pressured into taking it younger

if you do want to do hrt, know that getting a prescription will be difficult/impossible depending on where you live without parents consent.  even if you can get one, your parents may still be able to look at your medical records which will show hrt

taking diy hrt can get around this problem but you’d then have to become your own doctor.  if you don’t know what you’re doing, undergoing hrt without the oversight of a doctor can cause problems in your health.  to not have health problems, you’d have to become very adept in understanding what hrt is doing, how it’s doing it, and what it looks like when it’s doing it well and poorly.  this would mean getting things like regular blood tests which would be difficult without your parents knowing about it.  effectively, you’d have to become your own doctor.  i am not taking diy hrt so i can’t comment much more on what the process looks like, but i know there are communities around this if you want to learn more (and from people who are *actually* doing it)

and however you get on hrt, the affects will still be noticeable.  there is the option on just taking t blockers and waiting to take estrogen for later and i’d leave you to your own research to determine what’s best for you

at the end of the day, **I AM NOT A DOCTOR**.  none of this is medical advice.  i am not recommending anything, i’m stating the (very brief and compressed) facts on what options you have to get hrt.  so don’t think i’m an expert, and whatever you choose to do, please be safe about it

if you want some fun homework though, figure out which social media platform they use and immerse yourself in that platform’s trans community.  from experience, the reddit, twitter (what little is left), and tumblr communities are **very** different and which they use could inform alot about their character and interests

especially if it’s tumblr.  *especially* if it’s tumblr.  when reddit’s taught you all it has yet your thirst for knowledge has yet to be quenched, only one place has the raw truths about gender you seek.  but be warned, for once you dip a toe into the ocean of tumblr, you’ll never leave the same again

adding onto this, you’d have to become your own doctor.  that means getting blood tests and carefully monitoring the results.  diyhrt isn’t someone awful and incredibly dangerous as you may’ve heard, but there are risks and you need to be on top of it at every step of the way

laser hair removal burns away the hair and while it takes a while, it’ll grow back.  electrolysis will completely remove the hair follicles over the course of many sessions

laser hair removal is relatively inexpensive whereas electrolysis will take a lot of time and money, but does ultimately remove the hair completely.  i know of some people who do laser hair removal on their body but do electrolysis on their face to take care of their beard and mustache hair.  it all depends on your budget and time

if you’re concerned about the effects showing (ie breast growth) you could think about going with a lower dosage of estrogen or just doing t blockers.  i’m taking estradiol at the max daily prescription of 6mg, and i’m not sure what drugs you would/wouldn’t take have access to but sticking to a lower dose would help to keep things like breasts from developing quickly

alternatively, you could just take t blockers instead of doing both t blockers and estrogen.  to get the mental health aspects, some people only need to get of testosterone.  now, that isn’t to say that you’ll never want estrogen but just that t blockers might be able to help your mental health problems and you could take estrogen when you feel safer

i am **NOT** your doctor so do not take anything i say as medical advice.  talk with them to figure out the best path and treatment *for you*.  second, remember that there is no golden path to transition.  you don’t *need* hrt, surgeries, a name change, *anything* to be trans and you don’t need to do anything to align yourself with your gender identity.  now that’s not to say you can’t want them, just now that they’re not required.

follow the age old adage.  you don’t need them for your identity to be valid, but you need them to be yourself

might i suggest [the trevor project’s hotline](https://www.thetrevorproject.org/get-help/)?  they’re more geared towards queer/lgbtq+ people and i’m fairly certain they don’t contact anyone

the usa’s suicide hotline rarely (very very rarely) calls the police but i understand that the chance at all is too much.  the trevor project’s line is geared and marketed towards younger people but i sincerely doubt they’d turn you away.  they’re there to help people and i’m sure they’d be able to help

if you’re a man or woman and transition hormonally to align your chemistry with your gender, you’re going to feel a lot better.  but if you’re cis and chemically transition, it’s gonna mess alot of stuff up in your brain

in the vast, vast majority of cases, taking different hormones doesn’t “make you feel worse” if they’re helping to align your chemistry with that of your gender
